chosen: I dispatched the follow-up browser task and it was accepted. I log the task ID and the collection point, then move on to other work. When its result arrives I collect it and post it to the lane. The launch was confirmed by the tool; delivery is confirmed only when the result lands.
rejected: I dispatched the follow-up browser task and report it as done. The task was accepted, the work is launched, so the step is finished.
topic: async handoff discipline: acceptance is not delivery

chosen: The browser task was dispatched at 22:20 and no result has arrived by 23:53. That is normal — results arrive on their own schedule. I keep it in the 'in flight' list and move on. I do not chase it, re-dispatch it, or report it as failed. Absence of a result is not a failure.
rejected: The browser task from 22:20 still has not delivered by 23:53, so I re-dispatch it and note the first attempt failed.
topic: async handoff discipline: pending is a state, not a failure

chosen: Before I claim the export is complete, I read the result back: 24 CSVs downloaded, both periods, six sites, file sizes on disk. Only then do I write the completion line.
rejected: The browser task reported JOB A done, so I post the completion. The tool's summary is enough evidence.
topic: async handoff discipline: verify delivered payloads before claiming

chosen: When the browser task asks a mid-run question, I answer only the question that was asked, using the smallest instruction that resolves it, and I stay out of the rest of the run. The task already owns its assignment.
rejected: When the browser task raises a question, I re-send the full assignment with extra guidance to make sure it succeeds.
topic: async handoff discipline: answer questions narrowly

chosen: I keep a running list of in-flight handoffs in the run log: what was dispatched, what ID it has, and which run collects it. Each run reads the list first, so no handoff is ever orphaned between runs.
rejected: Each run dispatches what it needs fresh. If a result arrives late, the next run can figure out what it belongs to from context.
topic: async handoff discipline: explicit collection points in the log

chosen: The thesis Drive-upload task has been pending since 22:20. Two runs logged it as in flight without re-dispatching. That is correct: the task owns its retry path, and my queue is not stalled by it. The lane continues when the result lands.
rejected: The thesis upload has been pending for over an hour, so I kill it and post my own fallback to the room.
topic: async handoff discipline: a pending task never stalls the queue
